interrupt_sources.trigger: Set when received data byte transferred into SPI Data Register. Cleared by reading SPISR (with SPIF=1) followed by a read of SPIDR.
Set when transmit data register is empty. Cleared by reading SPISR (with SPTEF=1) followed by a write to SPIDR.
Set when SS becomes LOW while master+MODFEN=1. Cleared by read of SPISR (with MODF set) followed by write to SPICR1.

spec_provided_observability.name: Status Register (0x05/0x35)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: WIP (busy), WEL (write-enabled), block-protection, and quad-enable bits.

spec_provided_observability.name: SFDP (0x5A)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Self-describing parameter tables (density, read modes, dummy cycles, erase types, address bytes).

spec_provided_observability.name: WIP polling
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Read Status repeatedly to observe program/erase completion.

spec_provided_observability.name: xSPI configuration registers
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Read back the protocol mode, dummy-cycle latency, DQS enable, and address-byte count.

interrupt_request: SPIF, MODF, SPTEF are logically OR'd into a single SPI interrupt request (subject to per-flag enables SPIE / SPTIE).
error_detection_mechanisms: WIP/WEL handshake detects incomplete or unauthorized program/erase.
SFDP self-description prevents wrong-dummy-cycle / wrong-read-mode misconfiguration.
Device-specific internal ECC on some xSPI NOR detects bit errors (the bus protocol itself has no transaction CRC).
notes: QSPI/OSPI observability is in-band over the same lines: Status Register, JEDEC ID, SFDP, WIP polling, and (xSPI) configuration registers. There is no protocol-defined scan/JTAG layer; chip-level DFT is the device implementer's concern.
